_schema.purpose: Shared cross-language fixture pinning path normalization + workspace_id join-key outputs. The Rust core is the source of truth; the Swift conformance stage asserts its own PathNormalizer.normalize / WorkspaceIdentity outputs against the `expected_*` fields for `must_agree` rows.
_schema.platform: macOS (paths are lowercased; normalize is case-insensitive)

row_fields.input: raw input path string fed to the normalizer / workspace_id
row_fields.divergence_reason: (only when documented_divergence) why Rust and Swift differ. Two distinct kinds exist: (a) INTENTIONAL/by-design divergence (e.g. '.'/'..' replay determinism) and (b) CURRENT cross-language drift that C2-Phase2 must reconcile. Rows of kind (b) carry a `phase2_reconcile` marker.
row_fields.phase2_reconcile: (only on documented_divergence rows of kind (b)) true => this is an UNINTENDED current workspace_id drift between Rust and Swift, rescued today only by runtime path-containment fallbacks, and is a C2-Phase2 reconcile target — NOT an intentional design divergence.
row_fields.expected_default_workspace_id: Rust default_workspace_id(input) = workspace_id(input, input) output (source of truth)

consumer_notes.rust: domain/identity.rs tests::corpus_pins_normalize_and_workspace_id reads this file relative to CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and asserts every static row (pins Rust's own outputs for ALL rows regardless of agreement, since Rust is the source of truth).
consumer_notes.swift: For must_agree rows, assert PathNormalizer.normalize(input) == expected_normalize and WorkspaceIdentity.fromPath(input) == expected_default_workspace_id. For documented_divergence rows, the Swift output is EXPECTED to differ; pin the CURRENT Swift value and assert the divergence still holds (do not assert equality with the Rust expected_*). The static rows use paths that DO NOT exist on disk, so both Rust canonicalize() and Swift resolvingSymlinksInPath() fall through to their lexical/string behavior, keeping the corpus deterministic across machines.
consumer_notes.fs_dependent: Git-worktree and symlink edges cannot be pinned to literal strings (they depend on a real tmpdir). They are described in `fs_dependent_cases` and exercised by Rust with live tmpdirs: the symlink edge by tests::corpus_fs_dependent_symlink_normalize_keeps_link_workspace_id_resolves and the worktree edge by tests::workspace_id_is_stable_across_worktrees. The Swift stage mirrors the symlink tmpdir construction in PathNormalizerConformanceTests; worktree stability is owned by the Rust test (see the symlinked_dir / git_worktree_stability rows below).

static_rows.description: plain absolute path, already lowercase, no trailing slash
single trailing slash: normalize AND workspace_id agree (C2-Phase2 reconciled)
static_rows.note: C2-Phase2 RECONCILED. Rust workspace_id now runs normalize_path_for_matching on BOTH the project_id and project_path BEFORE hashing (STEP 1b), so a trailing slash is stripped before the source string is built and this row collapses onto plain_abs (5d699b305e97dd1568da5aaf1ec9a3ab). Swift WorkspaceIdentity.fromPath already normalized first, so both sides now agree. Previously this drifted (Rust hashed the RAW '/users/pete/code/myrepo/|/users/pete/code/myrepo/' -> 973dca301891a37acca11bbb72cebfaa) and was rescued only by runtime path-containment fallbacks.

static_rows.description: double trailing slash: normalize AND workspace_id agree (C2-Phase2 reconciled, same root cause as trailing_slash)
static_rows.note: C2-Phase2 RECONCILED. Same fix as trailing_slash: STEP 1b normalizes the inputs (collapsing the double slash) before hashing, so this collapses onto plain_abs (5d699b305e97dd1568da5aaf1ec9a3ab) and matches Swift. Previously Rust hashed the RAW '/users/pete/code/myrepo//|/users/pete/code/myrepo//' -> cf208ebfda766c2ba02fc9787c1b986a.

static_rows.description: filesystem root must survive trailing-slash stripping
mixed-case path lowercases to match plain_abs
static_rows.note: normalize AND default_workspace_id match plain_abs exactly: case-insensitivity is the whole point of the lowercase step.

static_rows.description: a '..' parent segment is NOT collapsed by Rust normalize_path_for_matching
static_rows.divergence_reason: Rust normalize_path_for_matching is a PURE STRING op (no FS, for replay determinism) and leaves '..' literal. Swift PathNormalizer.normalize runs URL.standardizedFileURL which LEXICALLY collapses '..', yielding /users/pete/code/myrepo. The two outputs differ by construction.
static_rows.note: Swift expected_normalize would be /users/pete/code/myrepo and Swift expected_default_workspace_id would equal plain_abs's 5d699b305e97dd1568da5aaf1ec9a3ab. The join is rescued at runtime by SessionStateManager path-containment fallbacks.

static_rows.description: a '.' current-dir segment is NOT collapsed by Rust normalize_path_for_matching
static_rows.divergence_reason: Same root cause as dotdot_segment: Rust leaves '.' literal (pure string), Swift URL.standardizedFileURL collapses it. Outputs differ by construction.

static_rows.description: a project_id ending in .git (the git-repo common-dir key) used as a bare input to default_workspace_id (C2-Phase2 reconcile target)
static_rows.note: C2-Phase2 reconcile target — now RECONCILED to must_agree. The Rust value is unchanged for THIS static (non-existent) input: default_workspace_id calls resolve_project_identity, which returns None for a path that does not exist on disk, so it falls back to workspace_id(input, input). repo_root_from_project_id detects the trailing '.git' file_name, strip_prefix(repo_root) leaves the relative segment '.git', and Rust hashes source '/users/pete/code/myrepo/.git|.git' -> ad22cc6998a67d53eb7896bc41da7925. The reconciliation that matters operationally is proven by the live-tmpdir test default_workspace_id_converges_to_git_aware_for_same_project (and the rust_internal_divergence block): for a REAL git repo, default_workspace_id resolves the .git common_dir + repo_root and converges onto the git-aware key, so the project-list key equals the session/routing key. As of C2-Phase2, Swift WorkspaceIdentity.fromPath is now .git-aware: it mirrors Rust's repo_root_from_project_id relative-rewrite (trailing '.git' file_name -> relative segment '.git') and hashes the same .git-relative source '/users/pete/code/myrepo/.git|.git', so Swift AGREES with Rust on ad22cc6998a67d53eb7896bc41da7925. The prior .git-unaware Swift value (f11988aa7d1c2ad9f893c462fef23134, from hashing '/users/pete/code/myrepo/.git|/users/pete/code/myrepo/.git') is no longer produced. This row is asserted EQUAL across both languages by the Swift testMustAgreeRowsMatchRust conformance test.

rust_internal_divergence.description: C2-PHASE2 RECONCILED. For the SAME git project, the pinned-project-list key (default_workspace_id of the repo path) now AGREES with the git-aware workspace_id(common_dir, repo_path), because default_workspace_id resolves project identity (git common_dir + repo_root) before hashing.
rust_internal_divergence.why: STEP 1: default_workspace_id(repo_path) now calls resolve_project_identity, which (for a REAL git repo) returns project_id = the .git common_dir and project_path = the repo_root, then hashes via workspace_id(common_dir, repo_root) -> the SAME source string and MD5 as the git-aware key the session/routing reducers compute (source '/users/pete/code/myrepo/.git|', relative empty after repo_root_from_project_id strips .git, -> cca950078b6f57529eb688528c2a4d7d). The project-list key and the session/routing key are now ONE key for a git project, so a pinned project joins its live session state without relying on path-containment fallbacks.
rust_internal_divergence.proof: Live-tmpdir Rust tests domain::identity::tests::default_workspace_id_converges_to_git_aware_for_same_project and default_workspace_id_agrees_with_git_aware_for_same_project_c2_phase2 build a real .git repo and assert default_workspace_id(repo_path) == workspace_id(common_dir, repo_root). The literal cca9... value here applies to a repo rooted at /Users/pete/Code/myrepo; the tmpdir tests assert the EQUALITY of the two derivations rather than a fixed hash, since the value is path-dependent.
rust_internal_divergence.note: The static literal paths could NOT demonstrate this convergence (resolve_project_identity returns None for non-existent paths and falls back to hashing the raw path twice), which is why the proof lives in the live-tmpdir tests. The pre-fix divergent default-of-repo-path value was 5d699b305e97dd1568da5aaf1ec9a3ab.

fs_dependent_cases.description: A linked git worktree (.git is a file with 'gitdir:' + commondir) must resolve to the SAME project_id/project_path as the primary worktree, so workspace_id is stable across worktrees.
fs_dependent_cases.construction: Build a tmpdir repo with .git/ dir + package.json marker, plus a sibling worktree whose .git FILE points at <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name> with a commondir of '../..'. resolve_project_identity on a file in each must yield equal project_id and project_path, and workspace_id over those must be equal.
fs_dependent_cases.expected: dynamic (tmpdir-relative); assert equality between the two worktrees rather than a literal hash.
fs_dependent_cases.note: Exercised by Rust tests::workspace_id_is_stable_across_worktrees (it builds the tmpdir repo + linked worktree and asserts equal project_id/project_path/workspace_id). A real git worktree (with a .git FILE + commondir) is impractical to construct deterministically in the Swift unit-test environment, so worktree stability is OWNED by that Rust test; the Swift conformance stage acknowledges the gap with an explained placeholder rather than re-deriving it.

fs_dependent_cases.description: A symlinked directory pointing at a real target.
fs_dependent_cases.divergence_reason: Rust normalize_path_for_matching does NOT resolve symlinks (pure string). Rust workspace_id calls std::fs::canonicalize which DOES resolve the symlink (FS-touching). Swift PathNormalizer.normalize calls resolvingSymlinksInPath when the file exists (FS+env-dependent). So normalize disagrees (Rust keeps the link path, Swift resolves it) while workspace_id may agree because both resolve the link via the FS. The exact behavior is machine/FS-dependent; this row documents the seam rather than pinning a literal.
fs_dependent_cases.expected: dynamic (tmpdir-relative); observe behavior, do not assert a literal.
fs_dependent_cases.note: Exercised by Rust tests::corpus_fs_dependent_symlink_normalize_keeps_link_workspace_id_resolves with a live tmpdir symlink: it pins that Rust normalize KEEPS the symlink path string (link != target) while Rust workspace_id canonicalizes THROUGH it (link == target). Mirrored on the Swift side by PathNormalizerConformanceTests.testSymlinkSeamMirrorsRust, which builds the same tmpdir symlink and pins the CURRENT Swift PathNormalizer.normalize + WorkspaceIdentity.fromPath behavior, cross-referencing the Rust finding to document the Rust-vs-Swift symlink seam.
